youtube.title: KATHRYN ENNIS-CARTER
youtube.summary: Public management adviser Kathryn Ennis-Carter joins Paul Brennan to examine the historical rivalries, religious divisions and geopolitical interests shaping the conflict in the Middle East. She argues that media coverage often overlooks key players and underlying tensions, including the Sunni-Shia divide, while focusing heavily on Donald Trump and Benjamin Netanyahu. Kathryn also discusses propaganda, political misrepresentation and the competing strategic interests of the United States, Europe and Middle Eastern powers. Catch up on this series: Part 1 | The Middle East’s Hidden Power Struggle Part 2 | Tracing the Deep Roots of the Middle East Conflict Think for yourself. Get RCR Bites FREE every weekday

youtube.title: STEVE KEEN
youtube.summary: Michael Arbon speaks with Professor Steve Keen, a distinguished research fellow at UCL, about Australia's reliance on imported fuel, the drivers of inflation and the risks of excessive household debt. They examine AI's potential to reshape employment, the decline of Australian manufacturing and the role of finance in housing unaffordability. Steve also challenges mainstream economic assessments of climate change, warning that the consequences of inaction could be catastrophic. Discover more from Steve on his website SteveKeen.com , YouTube and X Find Michael on Facebook and X

youtube.title: HARRY MOWBRAY
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan speaks with businessman and organic farmer Harry Mowbray about his vote-splitting strategy to create a parliamentary overhang and strengthen the centre-right under MMP. They debate wasted party votes, coalition politics and electoral reform, before turning to economic growth, personal responsibility and the risks of genetic engineering to organic farming, including cross-pollination and liability for contamination.
